w: After his morning puja, Swamishri performed pujan of bricks for the foundation of a new Hari mandir in the village of Kudiyara..
During lunch, Swamishri viewed a video of the murti sthapna celebration of Bhandut.
In the evening, Swamishri departed for navsari, arriving there at 6.45 pm.

After the evening discourse on the Kathopanishad by Pujya Viveksagar Swami, satsangi youths of Chennai performed a drama ‘Aj Sudhre Avtikal'. Swamishri blessed the assembly providing solutions to today's family problems.

After his meal, Pramukh Swami Maharaj spoke on the phone with students in Bangalore. These students had observed vows, austerities and fasts for Swamishri's health. Swamishri said to them, "All of you are studying, so may you study as well as possible, and along with that may the values of satsang you have become especially firm. May you not forget what you have learnt when you go out. May you not forget satsang, puja and prayers either; these are my blessings. Be vigilant that no addiction or vice creeps in. Giving others the satsang you have received here, and giving values to others too, is a great seva. We pray to Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj that you have special success in the degrees you have received and that you can bring others into satsang."
Brahmvihari Swami said, "Nowadays no one has the patience to read so many letters; only you read them calmly. In this day and age no one does this. You finished all of today's post today itself."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "It is finished today, but more will come tomorrow, won't it!"
Dharmacharan Swami said, "The fax machine is always on; faxes keep coming."
Abhayswarup Swami said, "Big faxes of seven or eight pages come from abroad; we get tired putting them in order; we lose patience."
Swamishri said, "It is exactly the kind of work in which one loses patience."

This morning when Mahant Swami Maharaj went to the mandir, in Harikrishna Maharaj's shrine the pujari sadhus held out a slate before him and asked him to write something. A sentence had already been written and placed there before Thakorji. Swamishri wrote that same sentence on the slate: "Egoism is great darkness."
Seeing this, the sadhus said, "Please sign below, Sa. Ke. (Sadhu Keshavjivandas)."
Then Swamishri said, "How is this sentence ours? It is someone else's."
What freedom from pretence in Swamishri!

This evening, during a spiritual discussion, Mahant Swami Maharaj was asked, "You knew 4 years beforehand that you would become the guru. Yet you did not let anyone even get a hint. And after becoming the guru, how much honour and comfort suddenly began to come to you! In such circumstances anyone else would burst with pride. But nothing like that is seen in you at all. With what thought do you stay like this?"
"Everything belongs to God; nothing is ours. Everything is God's and is to be given back to God. In between, we are agents." Swamishri revealed the secret of his humility and detachment.
